nodes.name: Hourly Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — every 1 h. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Gather from Airtable
nodes.notes: Searches Airtable's 'Tickets' table by formula (={LastModified} > DATEADD(NOW(), -1, 'days')) for records the pipeline hasn't handled yet. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Gather API Numbers
nodes.notes: GET https://api.example.com/v1/tickets — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Blend Sources
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Roll Up KPIs
nodes.notes: Group-by + aggregate (like a pivot table) — turns raw rows into KPI numbers.

nodes.notes: Single fixed LLM step (no tool choice) — cheaper and more predictable than an agent. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build an HTML digest table from the aggregated rows Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.notes: Creates a new record in Airtable's 'Tickets' table. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Record Sub-workflow Result
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 50 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

# Collect customer feedback with Airtable and Jira

**Pattern:** Survey & Feedback · **Level:** Architect · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## What it does
Collect customer feedback with Airtable and Jira. It runs automatically on a schedule.

## Why it exists
Manual escalation is slow and error-prone; this workflow makes the process repeatable, monitored and hands-off, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow
Hourly Schedule → Gather from Airtable → Blend Sources → Roll Up KPIs → Write Executive Summary (AI) → Compose HTML Report → Send Report via Slack → …

## Use it for
- Teams that want to survey & feedback without manual effort
- Anyone automating escalation in customer support
- Replacing a fragile manual process with a reliable workflow

## You get
- Standardizes the process every time
- Responds in seconds
- Scales without extra headcount

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Airtable PAT; Anthropic API key; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

KPIs are rolled up with Summarize (exact group-by + aggregate) before any AI touches the data — asking an LLM to 'figure out the numbers' from raw records is slower, costlier, and less reliable than doing exact arithmetic in n8n and only asking the model to narrate numbers that are already correct.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add a second data source and watch it blend into the same report via Merge.
2. Toggle the AI executive-summary step on and off and compare the report's usefulness.
3. Change the KPI grouping field and see how the pivot reshapes.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Anthropic API key**
console.anthropic.com → Settings → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Requires purchased credit.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your escalation process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
